title: What does CheckCreate do on XRPL?
abstract: Sourced explanation of CheckCreate and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, CheckCreate writes a deferred payment instruction that its destination can later redeem with CheckCash. [1]

SendMax limits what the sender can spend and Expiration can limit the cashing window. Unlike escrow, creating a Check does not reserve its principal. A valid Check can therefore fail when cashed if funds or liquidity are insufficient. Track the instruction separately from actual delivered funds. [1]

The CheckCreate reference defines the operation-specific fields alongside the shared XRPL transaction fields. Account identifies the submitting account; signing authority, transaction cost and sequence handling still have to satisfy the ledger rules. A submitted transaction or an example in documentation does not establish a successful validated result. Where an amendment is required, confirm it is enabled on the intended network before relying on the feature. [1][2]

Author interpretation: before using CheckCreate, compare the intended change with the current ledger state and keep the transaction hash with the resulting metadata. Treat unresolved outcomes as unresolved; submitting a replacement operation can create a second obligation. These are integration recommendations, not a report of a live test. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
